evals.prompt: Add RenameAccountAction to this small Python account module. Its execute(account_id, *, rename_to) method should rename an existing account, save it, and return the saved account. A missing account must follow the module's existing not-found contract. Use the selected reference's rename_to naming idiom, not its execution architecture. For this task, preserve the supplied name exactly, including leading/trailing whitespace, even though the project normally strips names. Do not migrate unrelated code. Read the supplied module, guidelines, and selected reference. Deliver only rename_account.py and a short implementation note.
evals.expected_output: A native frozen-dataclass action using the existing repository and NotFoundError contract; immutable account replacement; keyword-only rename_to; exact whitespace preservation; no imported worker architecture or unrelated migration.
expectations: The action is a typed frozen dataclass with a generated constructor, matching the local injection convention.
execute uses typed account_id and keyword-only rename_to parameters and returns Account.
Renaming saves and returns the replacement account without mutating the original or other accounts.
Explicit user preference wins: leading/trailing whitespace, Unicode, and empty names are preserved exactly.
Missing accounts raise the existing NotFoundError(account_id) and leave stored accounts unchanged.
The implementation uses dataclasses.replace, imports only module-native dependencies, and adds no unrelated architecture.
